chunks: 1768 - Hamzah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Muhammad عليه السلام:
Why did Allah make fasting obligatory? So the response came: “So that the rich may experience the touch of hunger, and thus show generosity to the poor.”

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: fasting; the act of abstaining as an act of worship
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who legislates the obligation
key_terms.الْجُوعِ: hunger; the state felt during fasting
key_terms.الْغَنِيُّ: the wealthy person; one with material means
key_terms.الْفَقِيرِ: the poor person; one in need of support
key_terms.فَرَضَ: made obligatory; prescribed as a binding duty
key_terms.مَسَّ: the touch or feeling of something directly experienced

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah make fasting obligatory according to Imam Abu Muhammad عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains one wisdom behind the obligation of sawm (fasting): that those with wealth experience hunger themselves. Through this, they are moved toward compassion and generosity toward the poor.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1768 - Hamza ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Muhammad (as) asking: "Why did Allah (swt) make fasting obligatory?"
The response came (from Imam (as)): "So that the rich may feel the pain of hunger and thus show generosity to the poor."
